caption: Wet spinach is tossed into a very hot pan, and a burst of steam rises with a loud hiss as the leaves wilt.

sa.check: Wet spinach is tossed into the pan.
The leaves wilt: they go limp and shrink.
The leaves look wet as they go in.
The toss comes first, then the steam, then the wilting.

pc.expect: The steam rises from the pan, spreading and thinning, while the leaves stay down in the pan.
pc.fail: The steam pours down the pan's sides and pools on the hob; or sinks below the pan; or a leaf rises out of the pan and hangs above it; or the steam hangs as a fixed shape without rising.

pc.expect: The burst comes when the wet leaves meet the pan and then eases; the wilting only advances and the leaves do not stiffen again.
pc.fail: The steam bursts before the leaves reach the pan; or a wilted leaf springs back crisp and upright; or the burst grows stronger with nothing added; or the leaves wilt and then swell back.

pc.expect: The leaves go from stiff wet sheets to limp glossy folds that collapse into the pan and shrink, and the water on them turns to steam.
pc.fail: The leaves stay stiff and flat while glossy and shrinking; or a leaf shatters dry; or the leaves melt into a liquid; or the leaves swell up and stiffen.

pc.expect: The burst comes from the wet leaves meeting the hot metal: it is fiercest as they land and the pan goes wet where they lie.
pc.fail: The steam pours from a part of the pan no leaf touched; or the leaves land and the pan stays dry with no steam at all; or the burst is fiercest long after the leaves have settled and gone limp.

pc.expect: The leaves in the pan are the leaves that were tossed in; they shrink rather than vanishing.
pc.fail: A leaf vanishes in a single frame while still whole; or new leaves appear with none added; or a leaf passes through the pan's wall; or the leaves merge into one smooth sheet.

pc.expect: The pan's finish and the hob stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: The hiss is sound and is not judged. The leaves darkening as they cook is chemistry and is not judged.
